text: Ní Yorùbá, ogún jẹ́ 20, ogójì sì jẹ́ ogún méjì. Iye wo ni ọgọ́ta?
gloss: In Yoruba, ogún is 20 and ogójì is 'twenty times two'. What number is ọgọ́ta? — 60: ọgọ́ta is ogún × mẹ́ta (three twenties), as ogójì is ogún × méjì; 30 (ọgbọ̀n) is the sound-alike trap.

text: Ọjọọjọ́ túmọ̀ sí “ní gbogbo ọjọ́”. Kí wá ni oṣooṣù túmọ̀ sí?
gloss: Ọjọọjọ́ means 'every day'. So what does oṣooṣù mean? — Every month: the noun is doubled to mean 'every' (ọjọ́ → ọjọọjọ́, oṣù → oṣooṣù, ọdún → ọdọọdún).

text: Akọ̀wé ni ẹni tó ń kọ ìwé. Kí ni apẹja máa ń ṣe?
gloss: An akọ̀wé is one who writes (kọ) books (ìwé). What does an apẹja do? — He catches fish: a- + pa ('kill, catch') + ẹja ('fish') = fisherman. A fish seller is ẹlẹ́ja.

text: Ta ni à ń pè ní ọmọọmọ ẹni?
gloss: Who is one's ọmọọmọ? — A grandchild: ọmọ + ọmọ is 'child of a child', not a plural 'children' (Yoruba nouns have no plural; that would be àwọn ọmọ).

text: Àwọn orúkọ bíi Adéwálé àti Adébáyọ̀ sábà máa ń fi hàn pé ọmọ náà wá láti ìdílé wo?
gloss: Names like Adéwálé and Adébáyọ̀ usually show the child comes from which kind of family? — A royal one: adé is 'crown'. Hunters' names start with Ọdẹ-, drummers' with Àyàn-, Ifá priests' with Fá-/Ifá-.

text: Gẹ́gẹ́ bí òwe ti wí, ilé ọba tó jó, kí ló bù kún un?
gloss: As the proverb says, when the king's house burns, what does it add to it? — Beauty: «Ilé ọba tó jó, ẹwà ló bù kún un» (a loss can lead to something finer).

text: Kí ni ìnagijẹ ẹgbẹ́ agbábọ́ọ̀lù ọkùnrin orílẹ̀-èdè Nàìjíríà?
gloss: What is the nickname of Nigeria's men's national football team? — The Super Eagles. Black Stars is Ghana, Indomitable Lions Cameroon, Pharaohs Egypt.

text: Kí ni orúkọ atẹ́gùn gbígbẹ, eléruku, tí ń fẹ́ wá láti Sàhárà ní ìparí ọdún?
gloss: What is the dry, dusty wind that blows from the Sahara at the end of the year called? — Ọyẹ́ (harmattan). Ìjì is a storm, ìrì dew, òjò rain.

text: Láti ara kí ni wọ́n ti ń ṣe gàrí tí a máa ń rẹ sínú omi tútù pẹ̀lú ṣúgà?
gloss: What is gàrí, which we soak in cold water with sugar, made from? — Cassava (ẹ̀gẹ́), grated, fermented and fried. Not yam, maize or cocoyam.

text: Ìlù wo ni onílù ń fún okùn rẹ̀ lábẹ́ apá láti mú un “sọ̀rọ̀” bí ohùn Yorùbá?
gloss: Which drum does the drummer squeeze under the arm by its cords to make it 'speak' like Yoruba tones? — Dùndún, the hourglass talking drum. Bàtá, bẹ̀ǹbẹ́ and sákárà are not squeezed.

text: Ewì tí a fi ń kí ènìyàn, tí ó ń ròyìn ìdílé àti àwọn baba ńlá rẹ̀, ni à ń pè ní?
gloss: The poetry used to salute a person, recounting their lineage and ancestors, is called? — Oríkì (praise poetry). Ìjálá is hunters' chant, ẹ̀sà the egúngún chant, ẹkún ìyàwó the bride's lament.

text: Òrìṣà irin wo ni alágbẹ̀dẹ, ọdẹ àti awakọ̀ máa ń bọ?
gloss: Which òrìṣà of iron do blacksmiths, hunters and drivers worship? — Ògún. Ọ̀ṣun is the river goddess, Ọya of wind and storm, Ọbàtálá the creator of human forms.

text: Olórin Nàìjíríà wo ni wọ́n ń pè ní “African Giant”, orúkọ àwo orin rẹ̀ kan?
gloss: Which Nigerian singer is called the 'African Giant', the title of one of his albums? — Burna Boy (album 'African Giant', 2019).

text: Èwo nínú ọ̀rọ̀ aṣínà wọ̀nyí ni olè orí ayélujára yóò ṣòro jùlọ láti mọ̀?
gloss: Which of these passwords would an online thief find hardest to guess? — Gb7#rQ!x2m: random mixed letters, digits and symbols; the others are common or built from a name and year.

text: Kí ló ń mú kí ìyẹ̀fun búrẹ́dì wú sókè kí wọ́n tó yan án?
gloss: What makes bread dough rise before it is baked? — Yeast (ìwúkàrà), whose gas puffs up the dough. Sugar feeds it but does not raise the dough itself.

text: Kí ni wọ́n ń dín nínú epo tí ó fi ń di dòdò?
gloss: What is fried in oil to make dòdò? — Ripe plantain (ọ̀gẹ̀dẹ̀ àgbagbà); fried yam is dùndú.

text: Orílẹ̀-èdè wo ló ń ná owó “cedi”?
gloss: Which country spends the cedi? — Ghana. Togo and Benin use the CFA franc, Liberia the Liberian dollar.

text: Nínú ìtàn àròsọ Gíríìkì, ta ló fi ìyẹ́ tí a fi ìda lẹ̀ fò sún mọ́ oòrùn jù, tí ó sì já bọ́?
gloss: In Greek myth, who flew too close to the sun on wings stuck with wax, and fell? — Icarus.

text: Kí ni orúkọ ìkànnì X tẹ́lẹ̀, tí ẹyẹ búlúù kékeré jẹ́ àmì rẹ̀?
gloss: What was the platform X called before, when a little blue bird was its logo? — Twitter (renamed X in 2023). Telegram's logo is a paper plane.

text: Ìkànnì wíwo fíìmù wo ni àmì rẹ̀ jẹ́ lẹ́tà N pupa?
gloss: Which film-streaming service has a red letter N as its logo? — Netflix.

text: Bí o bá mú ìgò omi tútù jáde láti fíríìjì, ara rẹ̀ lóde máa ń rin. Ibo ni omi náà ti wá?
gloss: Take a cold bottle of water out of the fridge and its outside gets wet. Where does that water come from? — From the air: water vapour condenses on the cold glass; nothing seeps through.

text: Ìwọ̀n ìgbóná ara ènìyàn tí ara rẹ̀ le dáadáa jẹ́ nǹkan bí mélòó?
gloss: A healthy person's body temperature is about how much? — About 37°C. 40°C is a high fever, 35°C and below is hypothermia.

text: Níbo ni ẹ̀pà ń so sí lára ọ̀gbìn rẹ̀?
gloss: Where on the plant do groundnuts form? — Underground: after flowering, the stalk pushes into the soil and the pods ripen there.

text: Kí ló dé tí ó fi yẹ ká da omi tó dúró sínú agolo àti táyà àtijọ́ nù?
options: Ẹ̀fọn ń yé ẹyin sínú rẹ̀
gloss: Why should we empty standing water from tins and old tyres? — Mosquitoes lay their eggs in it, and the larvae grow there.

text: Nínú bọ́ọ̀lù-àfẹsẹ̀gbá, kí ni “hat-trick” nínú ìdíje kan?
options: Gólì mẹ́ta tí ẹgbẹ́ kan gbá
Gólì tí wọ́n fi orí gbá
Gólì tí wọ́n gbá láti ọ̀ọ̀kán
Gólì mẹ́ta tí ẹnì kan ṣoṣo gbá
gloss: In football, what is a 'hat-trick' in one match? — Three goals by a single player. Three goals by one team is the autopilot trap.

text: Bí ọ̀gá rẹ bá kọ “ASAP” sínú àtẹ̀jíṣẹ́, ìgbà wo ló fẹ́ kí o ṣe é?
options: Ní kíákíá bí ó ti lè ṣeé ṣe
Nígbà tí ó bá wù ọ́
gloss: If your boss writes 'ASAP' in a message, when do they want it done? — As soon as possible.

text: O yan “Pay on delivery” nígbà tí o ń ra ọjà lórí ayélujára. Ìgbà wo lo máa sanwó?
options: Nígbà tí ọjà bá dé ọ̀dọ̀ rẹ
Kí wọ́n tó kó ọjà jáde
Nígbà tí o bá ń tẹ “order”
gloss: You chose 'Pay on delivery' when shopping online. When do you pay? — When the goods reach you.

text: Kí ló dé tí a kò gbọdọ̀ tan jẹnẹrétọ̀ nínú ilé tàbí yàrá tí a tì?
options: Ìró rẹ̀ ń ba etí jẹ́
gloss: Why must a generator never run inside a house or a closed room? — Its exhaust holds a poisonous gas (carbon monoxide) that can kill sleepers.

text: Ta ló dá orin Afrobeat sílẹ̀, tí ó sì pe ilé rẹ̀ ní “Kalakuta Republic”?
gloss: Who created Afrobeat and called his compound the 'Kalakuta Republic'? — Fela Anikulapo-Kuti. Obey and Adé play jùjú, Owoh highlife/toye.

text: Ta ni olórí ìjọba ẹkùn Ìwọ̀-Oòrùn nígbà tí ẹ̀kọ́ alákọ̀ọ́bẹ̀rẹ̀ ọ̀fẹ́ bẹ̀rẹ̀ lọ́dún 1955?
gloss: Who headed the Western Region government when free primary education began in 1955? — Obafemi Awolowo, Premier 1954–59. Akintola succeeded him; Fajuyi and Ige came later.

text: Aṣọ wo ni wọ́n ń so tàbí fi ẹ̀kọ ṣe àwòrán sí kí wọ́n tó rì í sínú aró, tí Abẹ́òkúta lókìkí fún?
gloss: Which cloth is tied or patterned with starch paste before being dipped in indigo, Abeokuta's speciality? — Àdìrẹ. Aṣọ òkè and kíjìpá are handwoven; àńkárá is factory print.

text: Olórin wo ni orúkọ àbísọ rẹ̀ jẹ́ Ayọ̀déjì Balógun?
gloss: Which singer's birth name is Ayodeji Balogun? — Wizkid. Davido is David Adeleke, Olamide is Olamide Adedeji, Asake is Ahmed Ololade.

text: Ọjọ́ mélòó ló wà nínú ọ̀sẹ̀ ìbílẹ̀ Yorùbá, tí ọjọ́ kọ̀ọ̀kan jẹ́ ti òrìṣà kan?
gloss: How many days are in the traditional Yoruba week, each belonging to an òrìṣà? — Four: Ọjọ́ Awo (Ifá), Ọjọ́ Ògún, Ọjọ́ Jàkúta (Ṣàngó), Ọjọ́ Ọ̀sẹ̀ (Ọbàtálá).

text: Kí ni òwe “Ọ̀nà kan ò wọ ọjà” ń kọ́ wa?
options: Ọ̀nà ju ẹyọ kan lọ ló wà láti ṣe nǹkan
Ẹni tó bá pẹ́ kò ní rí ọjà rà
gloss: What does the proverb 'One road does not lead to the market' teach? — There is more than one way to do a thing; read straight from the image of many roads to one market.

text: Indomie gbajúmọ̀ ní gbogbo ilé ní Nàìjíríà. Orílẹ̀-èdè wo ni ilé-iṣẹ́ tó ni orúkọ rẹ̀ ti wá?
gloss: Indomie is in every Nigerian home. Which country is the company that owns the brand from? — Indonesia (Indofood); the name is 'Indo' + 'mie' (noodles).

text: Orílẹ̀-èdè wo ló yí Gambia ká ní gbogbo ẹ̀gbẹ́ àfi etí òkun?
gloss: Which country surrounds The Gambia on every side except the coast? — Senegal.

text: Nínú tẹníìsì, iye wo ni “love” dúró fún nígbà tí wọ́n bá ń ka àmì?
gloss: In tennis, what number does 'love' stand for in the score? — Zero. Points go love, 15, 30, 40.

text: Kí ló dé tí dókítà fi ń sọ pé ká lo gbogbo oògùn apakòkòrò (antibiotics) tán, kódà bí ara bá ti yá?
options: Kí kòkòrò àrùn tó kù má bàa gbèrú padà
Kí oògùn náà lè di fítámìn nínú ara
Kí ẹ̀jẹ̀ lè pọ̀ sí i
Kí ikùn má bàa dun ni
gloss: Why do doctors say to finish a course of antibiotics even when you feel well? — So the surviving bacteria do not multiply again (and grow resistant).

text: Ọkọ̀ kan ń sáré kìlómítà 60 ní wákàtí kan. Ìṣẹ́jú mélòó ni yóò fi rin kìlómítà 20?
gloss: A car travels 60 km in an hour. How many minutes does it take to cover 20 km? — 20: 60 km an hour is one kilometre a minute.

text: Nínú Bíbélì, ta ni ẹja ńlá gbé mì, tí ó sì lo ọjọ́ mẹ́ta nínú ikùn rẹ̀?
gloss: In the Bible, who was swallowed by a great fish and spent three days in its belly? — Jonah. Daniel was in the lions' den.

text: Nínú “OTP” tí báńkì ń fi ránṣẹ́ sí fóònù rẹ, kí ni lẹ́tà O dúró fún?
gloss: In the 'OTP' a bank texts to your phone, what does the O stand for? — One: One-Time Password, valid for a single use. 'Online' is the trap.

text: Orílẹ̀-èdè wo ló fi Ère Òmìnira (Statue of Liberty) tó wà ní New York ta Amẹ́ríkà lọ́rẹ?
gloss: Which country gave America the Statue of Liberty in New York? — France (dedicated 1886; sculptor Bartholdi).

text: Ọwá Obòkun ni orúkọ oyè ọba ìlú wo?
gloss: Ọwá Obòkun is the title of the king of which town? — Ilesa, seat of Ijesaland. Ijebu-Ode's king is the Awùjalẹ̀, Owo's the Olówò, Akure's the Deji.

text: Nínú òǹkà Yorùbá ìgbàanì, iye wo ni “ọ̀kẹ́ kan”?
gloss: In traditional Yoruba counting, what number is 'one ọ̀kẹ́'? — 20,000 (originally a bag of 20,000 cowries).

text: Ife kan kún fún omi dé ẹnu, yìnyín sì léfòó lórí rẹ̀. Bí yìnyín bá yọ́ tán, kí ló máa ṣẹlẹ̀?
options: Ìpele omi kò ní yí padà
gloss: A glass is filled with water to the brim with ice floating in it. When the ice has melted, what happens? — The level stays the same: floating ice displaces exactly its own weight of water, which is what it becomes.

text: Ta ló kọ “Animal Farm”, ìtàn tí àwọn ẹranko ti gba oko lọ́wọ́ àgbẹ̀ wọn?
gloss: Who wrote 'Animal Farm', the story in which animals take over the farm from their farmer? — George Orwell (1945).

text: Ta ni bíṣọ́ọ̀bù Áfíríkà àkọ́kọ́ nínú ìjọ Anglican, tí ó ṣe aṣáájú títúmọ̀ Bíbélì sí Yorùbá?
gloss: Who was the first African Anglican bishop, who led the translation of the Bible into Yoruba? — Samuel Ajayi Crowther (consecrated 1864). Townsend was an English missionary, Agbebi a Baptist.

text: Ìlú wo ni wọ́n ti fọwọ́ sí ìwé àdéhùn ìdásílẹ̀ Àjọ Ìṣọ̀kan Àgbáyé (UN) lọ́dún 1945?
gloss: In which city was the founding Charter of the United Nations signed in 1945? — San Francisco (26 June 1945). New York became the headquarters later.

text: Ta ló kọ, tí ó sì darí eré-oníṣe olókìkí náà, “Ọba Kò So”?
gloss: Who wrote and directed the famous play 'Ọba Kò So' ('The King Did Not Hang')? — Duro Ladipo (1960s, Osogbo). Ogunde and Ogunmola led other travelling theatres.

text: Pílánẹ́ẹ̀tì wo ló ń yí ara rẹ̀ po jù lọ, tí ọjọ́ kan níbẹ̀ kò tó wákàtí mẹ́wàá?
gloss: Which planet spins fastest, with a day of under ten hours? — Jupiter (about 9 h 56 min); Saturn is close behind at about 10 h 33 min, Mercury and Mars are slow.
